title: From Chole Kulcha to Rogan Josh: Australian Couple's One-Day Amritsar Food Run Wins the Internet
excerpt: The couple hit Pehelwan Kulcha, Beera Samosa Wala, Gian Di Lassi and Surinder Meat Shop in a single day — and say it's only day one of their journey.
body:
• An Australian couple documented a single-day street food tour across Amritsar on Instagram, sampling the city's most celebrated dishes from breakfast to dessert.
  • Their stops included Pehelwan Kulcha, Beera Samosa Wala, the heritage shop Gian Di Lassi, Surinder Meat Shop and Rana Fruit Cream.
  • From chole kulcha and peda lassi to mutton rogan josh with extra gravy, the video has drawn enthusiastic reactions — and plenty of food-envy — from viewers.
  • The tour is only day one of the couple's journey, with more stops expected.

Indian street food has a way of stopping foreign travellers in their tracks, and one Australian couple has just given the world a full tour of Amritsar's famous food scene. In a video shared on Instagram, the couple spent an entire day working their way through the holy city's most loved food spots — from spicy chole kulcha and creamy lassi to rich rogan josh — and told followers this was only day one of their journey.

Breakfast at Pehelwan Kulcha

The day began at Pehelwan Kulcha, where they tried Amritsar's celebrated kulcha for breakfast. The couple praised its crispy, buttery texture served with chutney — the tandoor-baked flatbread stuffed with spiced potatoes that has made Amritsar a pilgrimage for food lovers. The next stop was Beera Samosa Wala, where they tucked into hot chole bhature and were struck by how light and soft the bhature was.

The lassi institution

No Amritsar food run is complete without lassi, and the couple headed to Gian Di Lassi, one of the city's old and well-known lassi shops. They tried the special peda lassi — the sweet milk-fudge mixed into the drink — and liked its rich, sweet taste. The regular lassi they found slightly sour, a flavour that reminded them of Greek yoghurt. For a city where lassi is served in tall glasses topped with a thick layer of malai, the comparison was high praise.

The tour continued with aloo tikki, whose crispy texture won them over; the spicy flavours, they said, made it even better than a regular hash brown. Then came the heavyweight stop: Surinder Meat Shop, where they ordered mutton rogan josh with extra gravy and found the meat soft and tender. To close out the day, they visited Rana Fruit Cream and declared the creamy dessert a fitting end to the tour.

Why Amritsar does this

Amritsar's food culture is inseparable from its identity. The city draws millions to the Golden Temple each year, and its old bazaars have fed pilgrims and travellers for generations — a cuisine built on tandoors, ghee, dairy and slow-cooked meats that Punjabi families have carried across the world. For the diaspora, spots like Gian Di Lassi are more than food stalls; they are landmarks of memory, the places parents describe when homesickness sets in.

That nostalgia was all over the comments. "You definitely had all the best ones," one viewer wrote. "I'm so jealous, omg," said another. "OMG. I want to do this so bad right now," read a third. Locals chimed in with recommendations — one urged the couple to try Ram Patty Kulcha, "one of the best patty kulchas around" — while another summed up the mood: "Watching this made me so happy — the pure nostalgia of going and just eating our way through Amritsar. Also, you have guts of steel cause ain't no way I be fitting all that in one day."

What to watch

The couple says this was only the first day, which means more Amritsar — and possibly more of Punjab — is on the way. Their itinerary so far reads like a greatest-hits list, and viewers are already lobbying for the next stops. If day one ended with rogan josh and fruit cream, day two has a lot to live up to.
